answer: The miller brands the wheel's axle with his own iron and counts the turns of the wheel for every sack that is ground, and the count is written in the mill book. A jetty sack ground on a neighbour's wheel fails the brand: at the voyage of the axle the turns must match the mill's own tally, and a strange wheel turns at another pace. Forging the count means running a mill for a season, bribing the miller and paying 11,800, while the juniper mark on the axle is checked at every grinding, so a sack whose turns were never counted is poured out.
